I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most on the North China Plain: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the land for the full year, match the local weather, and make use of the irrigation and field work I already know. I will put all my land into this wheat-maize rotation instead of trying something riskier, because I want steady grain, simpler management, and lower chance of losing money. For wheat, I will use improved seed, do a rotary tillage seedbed, give moderate fertilizer with more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, irrigate a few key times, and spray only when disease or insects are likely. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant hybrid summer maize, keep fertilizer a little heavier on nitrogen, irrigate in the main dry periods, and control weeds and insects with limited but timely pesticide use. I am choosing this plan because it fits my age, labor capacity, local experience, and the conditions in Hebei, and because it gives me reliable yield across the whole year.
